clue.text: Weed found in wild under logs

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of the words beside it running out of control into a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener finds a weed growing untamed beneath some logs.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundsel is a common yellow-flowered garden pest plant, a classic example of a weed.

clue.text: Robot's function on lunar excursion module

parts.note: to go is to function or work, as a machine does
LEM is the abbreviation for the Apollo lunar excursion module

explanation.surface: A robot's role aboard the spacecraft that lands on the Moon.
explanation.walkthrough: In Jewish folklore a golem is a clay figure brought to life to serve its maker, hence an automaton.
explanation.definitionFit: A golem is an animated man-made figure, an automaton that obeys orders, so it serves as a robot.

clue.text: Attentive pupil' once needing help

parts.note: a former pupil of a school is an old boy, OB
a help is a domestic servant

explanation.surface: A diligent former schoolboy who still needs assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe after 'pupil' is a stray mark in the printed text and plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone observant notices everything, which is to be watchful and attentive.

clue.text: Club near West End with best set-up

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near

indicators.note: the end of the word West is its final letter
in a down clue set up means the word for best is written upwards, so backwards

parts.note: tops is slang for the best

explanation.surface: A club close to London's West End offering the finest arrangements.
explanation.walkthrough: The West End is London's theatre and nightlife district, but here 'West End' is just the last letter of West. 'set-up' turns TOPS into SPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub, a venue for late-night entertainment, is a type of club.

clue.text: Sort of post originally received? I'll say!

definitions.text: Sort of post originally received? I'll say!

parts.words: Sort of post originally received? I'll say!
parts.note: a kind of postal service, but also read as an exceptional way of uttering words when they were first heard

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims about the unusual mail that arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: Delivery is also the manner of saying a speech, so a remarkable way of speaking lines is a special one as well as a premium postal service.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Mail's guaranteed next-day service is a named category of post.

clue.text: She controls men's organisation? That's a mere illusion

indicators.note: organisation means the letters of the words before it are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A woman who runs the men's group insists it is all a delusion.
explanation.walkthrough: A mere is a lake, so 'a mere illusion' is a lake's imaginary creature, not just a trick of the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous beast said to live in a Scottish lake has never been proven, so it is a lake phantom.

clue.text: Shout half-heartedly downstairs

indicators.note: half-heartedly means half of the double letter at the heart of the word for shout is dropped

parts.note: to bellow is to shout

explanation.surface: Someone yells feebly up from the ground floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Downstairs means on a lower floor, beneath, so it is an adverb of position like underneath.

clue.text: Dashing young chap, about to experience life

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the outside of the other

parts.note: to be is to exist, to have life
a lad is a young chap

explanation.surface: A stylish youth who is just about to live life to the full.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the whole picture: a blade is old slang for a dashing young man about town.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade is a dated term for a spirited, fashionable young man, a swaggering gallant.

clue.text: High, having' been turned on?

definitions.meaning: switched on and glowing, as a lamp is

explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe after 'having' is a stray mark in the printed text.
explanation.definitionFit: Lit up is slang for drunk and also describes something illuminated after being switched on.

clue.text: Drink spilt on TV, at end of kids' programmes

definitions.text: on TV, at end of kids' programmes

parts.note: water is something to drink
shed means spilt, as with tears or blood

explanation.surface: Someone knocks a glass over the television when the children's shows finish.
explanation.walkthrough: The watershed is the 9pm point on British television after which programmes unsuitable for children may be shown.
explanation.definitionFit: In UK broadcasting this is the evening cut-off time before which adult content is barred.

clue.text: Way to dip into baked dish

indicators.note: into says the second word's synonym goes inside the first's

parts.note: a lane is a way or road
to sag is to dip

explanation.surface: A method for dunking something into a casserole.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is an Italian pasta dish layered with sauce and cooked in an oven.

clue.text: Line delivered in film by one-time singer

indicators.note: delivered in means the letter is placed inside the other word

parts.note: a coat is a thin film or layer
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A movie in which a former vocalist speaks a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one-time singer' suggests a has-been pop star; the singer is a songbird and 'one-time' is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The coal tit is a small songbird, and crosswords often call birds singers.

clue.text: It's worth taking part in some rituals

indicators.note: taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: It's worthwhile joining in with certain ceremonies.
explanation.definitionFit: Merit is value or excellence, the quality of deserving praise.

clue.text: Mind being in the clutches of private landlord

indicators.note: in the clutches of means one piece is gripped inside another

parts.note: inner means private, as in one's inner thoughts
to keep, as in keep the shop, is to mind it

explanation.surface: A landlord's thoughts are held captive by a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private' looks like a soldier; it means INNER.
explanation.definitionFit: The keeper of a pub or inn is its landlord, the licensee who runs it.

clue.text: Duck puts bill back in to drink

indicators.note: in means the reversed bill sits within the word for drink

parts.note: to sup is to drink

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation for bill is read in reverse

parts.note: AC, account, is a bill

explanation.surface: A duck slips its beak into the water to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' looks like a duck's beak; it is an account, AC, turned to CA.
explanation.definitionFit: The scaup is a diving sea duck of northern waters.

clue.text: Temporary lodger's therefore put right at end of short passage

indicators.note: at end of places the letter for right after the shortened passage

parts.note: so means therefore

indicators.note: short means the last letter of the word for passage is cut off

parts.note: a journey is a passage from one place to another

explanation.surface: A guest staying briefly is moved to the end of a corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: A sojourner stays somewhere for a short time, a visitor rather than a resident.

clue.text: Frantic to get on the French road leading to the Channel

parts.note: la is French for the (feminine)
ST, street, is a road
the Ditch is old slang for the English Channel

explanation.surface: A desperate traveller takes the French road down to the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A last-ditch attempt is a desperate final effort, made in frenzy.

clue.text: Sailors found playing cards twice

parts.note: a deck is a pack of playing cards
hands are sets of playing cards dealt to players

explanation.surface: Sailors are discovered at a game of cards for the second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Deckhands are crew members of a ship, ordinary seamen.

clue.text: A' conductor to watch, popular one

parts.note: to scan is to watch closely
in means fashionable or popular
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A conductor worth seeing, liked by the crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe after 'A' is a stray mark in the printed text. Arturo Toscanini was a famous Italian conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was a celebrated Italian orchestral maestro.

clue.text: Harassed setter in trouble — exhausted by Jumbo?

indicators.note: in means the shuffled word sits inside the word for trouble

parts.note: a jam is a difficult situation, trouble

indicators.note: harassed means the letters of setter are flustered into disorder

explanation.surface: The puzzle-maker, stressed and in difficulty, is worn out by an elephant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumbo' suggests an elephant, but it is a jumbo jet, and 'exhausted' means blown out as engine exhaust, not tired.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet stream is a stream of gas expelled by a jet engine, as from an airliner.

clue.text: Considered as a future job prospect

definitions.text: Considered as a future job prospect

parts.words: Considered as a future job prospect
parts.note: seems to describe a candidate for employment, but means a building inspected by a burglar planning a robbery

explanation.definitionFit: To case a joint is criminal slang for reconnoitring premises before a robbery.

clue.text: Operatic part turned into a dreadful wailing

indicators.note: turned means the opera role's name is written backwards

parts.note: Lulu is the title role of Berg's opera

indicators.note: dreadful signals the letters of into a are jumbled

explanation.surface: A role in an opera is transformed into a terrible howling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses LULU to ULUL; 'dreadful' scrambles INTOA into ATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Ululation is a howling or lamenting cry, a loud wail.

clue.text: Have grouse after missing starter, say

indicators.note: missing starter means the first letter of the word for grouse is dropped

parts.note: to mutter is to grumble or grouse

explanation.surface: A diner complains after skipping the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grouse' looks like the game bird; it is the verb to complain.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter is to speak, voice or pronounce something.

clue.text: Use a screen when speaking

indicators.note: when speaking says the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a veil is a screen

explanation.surface: Employ a partition when giving a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Avail as a noun means benefit or use, as in to no avail.

clue.text: Firm investing nothing in store

indicators.note: investing means wrapping round, as clothing invests a body

parts.note: hard means firm
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A company puts no money into a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company; it is HARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoard is a hidden stockpile, a stash.

clue.text: Run into pack of Americans producing trash

indicators.note: into means the letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: deck is the American word for a pack of cards
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Bumping into a group of Americans results in rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreck is Yiddish-derived slang for rubbish or worthless junk.

clue.text: Fruitcake found in biscuit container

parts.note: a nut is a small biscuit, as in ginger nut
a case is a container

explanation.surface: A fruitcake turns up in the biscuit tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruitcake is slang for an eccentric or crazy person, a loony.

clue.text: What's fashionable in steel?

indicators.note: fashionable read as fashioned or shaped means the letters are reformed

explanation.surface: A question about what is currently trendy in the metal industry.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: steel is known for its strength under tension.
explanation.definitionFit: Tensile strength is the key property measured in steel, its resistance to stretching.

clue.text: Country's leaders, in referendum, ultimately right at last

indicators.note: leaders means the first letter of each of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: A nation's politicians, voting on a plebiscite, finally get it right.
explanation.definitionFit: Country used as an adjective, as in country life, means rustic, of the countryside.

clue.text: Measure court's taken before crook appears

parts.note: a yard is a courtyard, a court
a shepherd's crook is a stick

explanation.surface: A tennis court is booked before a criminal shows up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crook' looks like a criminal; it is a shepherd's staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardstick is a standard by which things are judged, a benchmark.
